author: Sofia Pahaoja

extraction.selected_components: Rim, hub and twelve spokes. Stand, drive belt, treadle and other components are excluded.
extraction.rotation: After subtracting the source origin, (x,y,z) becomes (-z,y,x), mapping the source X axle to local Z without a reflection.

separated_components.runtime_mount: One centered hub/spoke mesh and two instances of the same rim mesh at local axle Z = -0.08 and +0.08 metres. The unchanged full rotor is retained for historical captures.

extraction.attributes: Source vertex shape and UV records retained; normals rotated and normalized. Triangle order retained. No simplification or discovery-weld vertex merging. Godot applies ordinary glTF import conversion and tangent generation.

wood_albedo.jpg.role: sRGB color, original provider JPEG with no resize or re-encoding

wood_center_albedo.webp.role: Derived center-only warm shadow lift from the unmodified provider JPEG, lossy WebP quality 0.82

wood_normal.webp.role: Linear OpenGL tangent normal, float Lanczos resize, vector renormalization and nearest RGB8 encoding

wood_arm.webp.role: Linear red occlusion, green roughness and blue metallic, float Lanczos resize and nearest RGB8 encoding

preparation.source_material: The original glTF material is double-sided with default unit color, metallic and roughness factors. Runtime preserves those factors and sidedness, using the selected packed maps.
preparation.data_delivery: Lossless WebP decodes to the exact prepared RGB8 pixels; no channel reorder, green flip or color-space conversion. Resizing does not preserve all original spatial detail.
preparation.center_color_recipe: opening/machine_detail_check.gd --prepare-wheel-center-color pins wood_albedo.jpg and adds (0.18, 0.11, 0.06) times (1 - 0.2126 R - 0.7152 G - 0.0722 B) squared to each sRGB pixel, clamped to one; Godot save_webp uses lossy quality 0.82. The original JPEG and geometry are unchanged.
preparation.budget_choice: The original one-kilopixel lossless data maps were also prepared and retained externally. The shipped half-resolution data maps fit the current shared source allowance without another lossy encoding of the photographed color.

runtime: The complete current eight-file resource set is required. Two source meshes use cached materials with shared normal and packed surface maps: one centered hub/spoke instance uses the derived color atlas, and two symmetric rim instances keep the provider color. Three-tile wheels retain the exact prepared geometry. Larger admitted wheels cache visual-only radial remaps: source rim outer radius stays fixed under the existing parent scale, while rim wall and timber hub grow with the square root of tile count relative to the three-tile wheel; spokes extend into the shifted inner rim. Source normals and tangents are transformed with the geometry, and source UVs remain. The old rotor files remain byte-identical for provenance and reproduction. Original paddle positions, spindle, native projected axis/motion, fixed stands and worked journal remain. Partial or superseded rosters are incomplete. Earlier retained images keep their original source and material qualifications. No source scene, skeleton, animation, collider or controller is instantiated.
limits: The square-root proportion is an experimental art default, not a structural strength or mechanical design rule. Source UVs still stretch around the longer circumference; texture density and level of detail need further work. The second rim adds 1,872 visual triangles per wheel versus the original single rotor, and generated size meshes add cache memory; GPU cost is unmeasured. The current native launcher captures raw source assets; packaged Godot exports are unverified. Isolated asset fixtures and passive renders do not establish human visual acceptance or native power behavior.
